title: One Gift, Two Prophets
surface: [Fantasy] A prophetic gift forces its user to state every benefit and drawback of an event whenever speaking. An ancient practitioner loses clients who dislike hearing bad news. A modern user obeys the same rule and never lies, yet becomes the favorite “clear thinker” of two opposing audiences. What changes?
solution: The modern user records complete predictions, honestly saying both sides. Only afterward are the recordings edited: positive portions go to one account and negative portions to another. The shared identity is concealed. Different audiences follow their preferred account and mistake a selection for the full view. The speaking rule remains intact; distribution changes.

facts.text: Complete predictions are recorded before positive and negative portions are separated by editing.
Two seemingly separate accounts show different portions to different audiences.
This is a fictional audience scenario, not a universal claim about platform recommendation systems.

unknowns: The platform, predictions and account names are unspecified.
hints: Does the rule control what is said or what an audience eventually hears?
What can happen to a recording after the speech is complete?
Two accounts each publish only one side of the same complete prediction.
